app.name: Wireless Lab
app.tagline: Follow a 5G base-station signal one step at a time.
nav.label: Screens
chain.label: Progress
stage.figure_pending: The figure appears here when the step finishes.
diagnostics.title: Causes and fixes
start.title: Follow a base-station signal step by step
start.lead: Choose where the signal comes from. Without any hardware you can still go all the way with a practice signal.
start.practice.title: Practice mode
start.practice.desc: Try the whole process with a computer-generated signal. No hardware needed.
start.file.title: Saved file
start.file.desc: Process an IQ file (SigMF) recorded earlier. The same file always gives the same result.
start.file.path: Path to the SigMF meta file
start.file.testbed: This file was recorded on my own testbed (allows random-access observation)
start.device.title: Device
start.device.desc: Receive a real signal with a connected SDR. Receive only; nothing is transmitted.
start.status.title: Readiness
start.status.lead: What is available on this computer.
start.recent.title: Recent sessions
start.recent.none: No sessions yet. Pick a task above to begin.
scan.where.title: Where should we look?
scan.where.lead: Pick a band or type a centre frequency.
scan.where.fixed.synthetic: The practice signal has a fixed band. Scan right below.
scan.where.fixed.file: A saved file has the band it was recorded in. Scan right below.
scan.where.fixed.device: Pick a band or type a centre frequency.
scan.freq.label: Centre frequency (MHz, optional)
scan.freq.error: Enter a number between 70 and 7125 MHz.
follow.need_scan: Find a cell with a scan first.
ntn.eyebrow: Where is the satellite now, and how late does its signal arrive?
ntn.title: Satellite position and timing
ntn.where.title: My location
ntn.where.lead: Distance and delay to the satellite depend on where you are.
ntn.need_sib19: Satellite calculations need SIB19. Go through Follow until SIB19 is received.
track.title: Changes over time
track.lead: Follows the chosen cell again at a fixed interval and records how the values change.
track.empty: Nothing recorded yet. Start tracking and the graph appears here.
track.changes.title: SIB19 change history
track.changes.lead: Fields whose value changed in a newly received SIB19.
sessions.title: Sessions
sessions.lead: Your runs so far. Reopen one to continue, or export a report.
sessions.name: Name
sessions.confirm_delete: Delete session "{name}"? Its saved IQ and results are removed and this cannot be undone.
settings.location.title: My location
settings.location.lead: Used as the default for satellite calculations. Stored on this computer only.
settings.device.title: Device settings
settings.device.lead: Defaults used when receiving with a device.
settings.device.name: Device
settings.thresholds.title: Thresholds
settings.thresholds.lead: The frequency-offset search range and the limits used to flag anomalies.
settings.doctor.title: Environment check
settings.doctor.lead: Checks that the needed programs and devices are ready. Nothing is installed or changed.
phone.title: What the phone sees
phone.lead: Reads the cell an Android phone connected by USB is using now, as a starting point for the SDR scan. Optional.
phone.mismatch: PCI differs from the SDR result
phone.follow: Follow this cell with the SDR
phone.need_device: An SDR device must be connected.
phone.status.no_adb: adb was not found. Install Android platform-tools to use this.
phone.status.no_device: No phone connected. Turn on USB debugging, connect the phone and read again.
phone.status.unparsed: The phone's output could not be understood. See the raw text below.
track.replay: The same signal is being re-read, so measured values stay the same and only orbit-derived values change.
oai.title: Record from the OAI satellite simulator
oai.desc: Receives a fresh signal from the OAI NTN base-station simulator running on this computer and opens it. A software signal; nothing is transmitted over the air.
oai.busy: Recording… (about a minute if the base station has to start)
oai.stopped: Base station off · it is started briefly and stopped again
oai.hint: On the satellite screen use latitude {lat}, longitude {lon} (directly below the simulated satellite).
oai.diagram.label: How the signal gets from the OAI simulator to this screen
oai.node.gnb.desc: Keeps broadcasting like a base station carried on a satellite. Band {band}.
oai.node.file.desc: Stores the received signal as is (marked as testbed).
oai.node.follow.desc: Decodes in order: find → sync → MIB → SIB1 → SIB19.
oai.phase.waiting: Waiting for the base station to start broadcasting…
oai.phase.stopping: Stopping the base station that was started…
concept.scan.label: Concept: look at each frequency slot in turn to find where a base-station signal rises
concept.ssb.label: Concept: pick one of the repeating sync blocks and align to its start
concept.mib.label: Concept: turn the PBCH inside the sync block into bits and read the MIB
concept.sib1.label: Concept: read SIB1 from the PDSCH that the PDCCH points to
concept.sib19.label: Concept: use the satellite position and velocity in SIB19 to get distance and delay to the receiver
spectrum.title: Spectrum status
spectrum.lead: Pick a device to see its details and measure how strong the signal is on each channel. Receive only; nothing is transmitted.
spectrum.plan.title: Where to look
spectrum.plan.hint_sim: A simulated device cannot retune, so the band stored in its file is split into 16 slices.
spectrum.plan.hint_real: Pick a band and click channels, or type a centre frequency and bandwidth below (any frequency works). Add places you watch often with +.
spectrum.stat.label: Value shown
spectrum.clipped: Some channels are clipping. Lower the receive gain.
spectrum.chart.label: Received power per channel
spectrum.chart.caption: Values are uncalibrated relative levels (dBFS), not absolute power (dBm).
spectrum.chart.caption_base: The horizontal marks are the saved baseline. A bar above its mark has risen by that much.
spectrum.col.name: Channel
spectrum.how.title: How it is measured
spectrum.how.dwell: Each channel is captured for {ms} ms, a power spectrum is computed, and the power inside the channel width is summed.
spectrum.how.mean: Mean: average power over the whole capture, 10·log10(mean |x|²).
spectrum.how.median: Median: median of the power in 1 ms blocks. Steadier for bursty signals; equals the mean for continuous ones.
spectrum.how.peak: Peak: the largest I/Q sample. Near 0 dB means the input is clipping.
spectrum.how.unit: dBFS is relative to the largest value the device can represent (0 dB). It changes with the gain.
spectrum.fact.source: Values not marked "reported" come from the capability table and may differ slightly from the actual device.
view.title: Choose a centre frequency and bandwidth
view.lead: Enter the centre frequency and width you want; this shows what is arriving in that band.
view.lead_sim: A simulated device cannot retune, so the band stored in its file is shown as is.
view.max_width: This device can show at most {mhz} MHz at once.
view.error.inputs: Enter the centre frequency and bandwidth as numbers.
view.caption.spectrum: The dark line is the mean over the capture; the light line is the strongest moment. A large gap means a bursty signal.
view.caption.waterfall: Left to right covers {ms} ms. Low frequency at the bottom; darker is stronger ({lo} to {hi} dBFS).
spectrum.how.smooth: The value shown is the median of the last {n} sweeps. It filters out one-off spikes but lags a few seconds.
spectrum.how.auto: Auto baseline: 8 s after starting, once recent values stay within 2 dB, that value is saved as the baseline. If it keeps moving, it is saved anyway at 15 s and marked.
monitor.unreachable: Greyed cells are frequencies this device cannot receive.
monitor.title: Watching {n} channels
monitor.lead: The selected channels are measured in turn; the median of the last {n} sweeps is shown.
monitor.raised: {names} rose more than {db} dB above baseline
monitor.rise.label: Rise over baseline
monitor.rise.caption: How far each channel is above its baseline. Channels more than {db} dB up change colour.
monitor.rise.none: The rise appears here once a baseline exists.
view.error.paused: The channel monitor is using the device. Stop it above first.
wifi.aps.find: Find nearby APs on selected channels
wifi.aps.hint: Each channel is heard for 0.25 s and beacons are decoded. Allow 2–3 s per channel.
wifi.aps.title: APs found
wifi.aps.none: No AP found on the selected channels. Raise the gain or try other channels.
wifi.usig.title: Actual transmit bandwidth (Wi-Fi 7)
wifi.usig.desc: Counts the transmit width announced in Wi-Fi 7 frame headers. More frames narrower than the operating width suggests some channels are blocked. Needs downlink traffic to a Wi-Fi 7 client.
wifi.usig.narrowed: Transmit width dropped from {from} to {to} MHz
wifi.usig.none: No Wi-Fi 7 downlink frames in the last 10 s.
sim.hint: Uses stored practice signals instead of a device.
sim.badge: Simulation · stored practice signals are replayed as if from a device
sim.no_real: No device connected. A USRP appears here a few seconds after you plug it in.
hub.connect.title: Connect a device
hub.connect.lead: Plug in an SDR (such as a USRP) over USB; it appears below after a few seconds.
hub.connect.skip_note: Without a device you can use practice mode, saved files, simulated experiments, and this computer's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth (Nearby). You will be notified when a device is plugged in later.
hub.arrived.title: A new device was registered
hub.mine.title: My devices
hub.mine.none_mode: Running without a plug-in device (SDR). This computer's own radios are still available.
hub.none_mode: Started without a plug-in device (SDR). Features that need an SDR are hidden; this computer's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth are available below.
home.title: What would you like to do?
home.lead: Press Receive or Transmit. Turn devices on or off below.
home.empty_hint: Without a device you can still practise with stored signals below.
home.task.nr.desc: Find a 5G or satellite base station and read its broadcast step by step. Receive
home.task.wifi.desc: Monitor 2.4 / 5 / 6 GHz channels, find nearby APs, see actual transmit width. Receive
home.task.view.desc: Choose a centre frequency and bandwidth and look at any band. Receive
home.task.bt.desc: Advertisements nearby devices broadcast (address, name, maker) and channel levels. Receive
home.task.tx.desc: Send a test signal in a closed setup. A confirmation appears every time
home.without.title: Practise with stored signals
home.without.lead: No device needed: practice signals, files you saved earlier, or the simulator let you follow a base station to the end.
home.sim.title: Simulated device
home.sim.desc: Replays a stored practice signal as if from a device, so you can rehearse the device flow.
monitor.shaky: {names}: waiting for a steady value before saving the baseline
wifi.live.desc: Every 2 s one of the watched channels is heard for 0.12 s and its beacons and frame headers are read. Payloads are not decoded. The level chart updates a little slower while this is on.
wifi.live.no_aps: No beacon yet. Each channel has to come round in turn; give it a moment.
wifi.kinds.title: Frame kinds seen (last 10 s)
tx.title: Send a signal
tx.lead: Sends a test signal from the USRP for a fixed time. A confirmation window appears every time.
tx.strip: This screen really transmits. Use it only in a closed setup such as a cabled or shielded one.
tx.unavailable: This installation has no transmit function.
tx.file.path: SigMF meta file path (repeats from the start)
tx.note: A test tone, a standard test signal, or a waveform file you provide can be sent. It stops by itself when the time is up, and the time, frequency and gain are logged.
tx.sending: Transmitting… (opening the transmitter takes about 10 s the first time)
tx.error.inputs: Enter the device, centre frequency, sample rate and length as numbers.
tx.warn.title: Check before transmitting
tx.warn.responsibility: You are responsible for anything you transmit (radio regulations and so on). Do not radiate without authorisation or interfere with anyone else's communication.
tx.warn.agree: I have read this and accept responsibility for this transmission.
tx.warn.closed: This is a closed setup (cabled or shielded), or a frequency I am authorised to use.
wifi.live.off: Live decoding is off. Tick the box above to turn it on.
ble.title: Nearby Bluetooth devices
ble.desc: Every 2 s one advertising channel (37, 38, 39) is heard for 0.25 s and the advertisements devices broadcast to everyone are read. Connections are not followed.
ble.none: No advertisement yet. Try raising the receive gain.
ble.col.name: Name
ble.note: Devices with a 'random' address change it periodically, so one device may appear on several rows.
ble.directed: Packets aimed at one device are only counted: {list}.
tx.pick.title: Which frequency?
tx.pick.hint: Click a channel to fill in the centre frequency and sample rate.
tx.rate.hint: The sample rate is the width you can send at once: at 1 MHz only signals within ±0.5 MHz of the centre can be made.
tx.waveform.tone.desc: A test tone is a plain sine wave sitting on one frequency, carrying nothing. It shows as a single sharp line in the spectrum. Use it to check that transmit works, how much the cable loses, and how far the frequency is off.
tx.waveform.standard.desc: A test signal built to the standard, for checking that the receiving side decodes standard signals. The payload is random data; nothing that poses as an AP or base station is made.
tx.waveform.file.desc: Sends a waveform file (SigMF) you made, repeating from the start.
tx.standard.hint.wifi: Ten 20 MHz data frames repeated with 1 ms gaps. Pick a Wi-Fi channel above.
tx.standard.hint.ble: A test advert named 'nrtrail-test' repeated every 5 ms. Pick a Bluetooth advertising channel (ch37, ch38, ch39) above.
tx.planned.wifi-mgmt: Wi-Fi management frames (beacon, channel switch announcement…)
tx.planned.note: 'Not built' slots have no generator in this tool. Put a generator (Python or MATLAB) with the same id in plugins/tx/ to enable one; the _template files there show how.
tx.plugin.hint: A signal made by a generator you placed in plugins/tx/.
hub.search.searching: Looking for devices… ({s} s so far; right after opening the program this can take about 30 s)
hub.search.busy: A USRP is plugged in but another program is using it: {list}. Close that program and search again.
hub.search.none: No device connected (checked {s} s ago). Check the USB cable and port.
hub.search.reset: Stop leftover processes and search again
hub.search.reset_hint: Press this if the device is not found or shows as busy. It stops every device helper this tool started (including ones from earlier runs or other windows), starts a fresh one and searches again. Other programs (GNU Radio etc.) must be closed by you.
hub.adapters.title: This computer's radios
hub.power_off: It is turned off. Turn it on in the operating system to use it.
home.adapters.title: This computer's radios
home.adapters.lead: Wi-Fi and Bluetooth adapters built into or plugged into this computer. Unlike an SDR, they give results decoded by the chip (lists of nearby networks and devices), not the radio signal itself.
home.task.near-wifi.desc: Which channels nearby networks are on and how strong. Listen only, no connection
home.task.near-bt.desc: Advertisements broadcast by nearby devices (name, maker, strength). Listen only, no connection
nearby.title: Nearby
nearby.lead: See what is being broadcast around you with this computer's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth. It does not connect to anything.
nearby.no_adapter: No usable Wi-Fi or Bluetooth adapter.
nearby.chart.alt: Bar chart of strength per channel in the {band} GHz band. {n} networks
nearby.wifi.title: Nearby Wi-Fi networks
nearby.wifi.hidden: The operating system hid network names and addresses. Channels and strength are still shown. To see names, allow this program (the terminal) in the operating system's location services settings.
nearby.wifi.current: Connected network: channel {channel} ({band} GHz), strength {rssi} dBm, noise {noise} dBm
nearby.wifi.note: Strength is the value reported by the adapter (dBm). On Windows and Linux it is estimated from the operating system's quality (%) as quality/2 − 100. ×n above a bar is the number of networks on that channel.
nearby.ble.title: Nearby Bluetooth devices
nearby.ble.note: Devices change their address periodically for privacy, so one device may appear on several rows. macOS shows a random identifier instead of the real address.
nearby.col.name: Name
nearby.limits: An adapter cannot show a spectrum, decode frame contents, or transmit. Those need an SDR device.
hub.sdr.title: Plug-in devices (SDR)
hub.adapters.always: These are already part of this computer, so you can use them even if you start without a device.
tx.rx.desc: While transmitting, the same frequency is received and compared with what was sent, to see whether the signal really went out. The receiving device may be another USRP or the same one.
tx.rx.wiring.two: Connect the transmitter's TX port to the receiver's RX port with a cable and an attenuator (30 dB or more recommended). A direct connection without an attenuator can damage the receiver.
tx.rx.wiring.same: Connect the TX port and the RX port (RX2) of the same device with a cable and an attenuator (30 dB or more recommended). Even unconnected, leakage inside the device may be weakly visible.
tx.rx.missing: The sent signal was not confirmed on the receive side
tx.rx.missing.hint: Check the cable, the receive gain and the receive port. If the level is at the floor, the signal did not reach the receiver.
tx.rx.tone.value: {found} kHz (sent at {expected} kHz), {db} dB above the floor
tx.rx.match.value: {v} (1 is identical; 0.3 or more counts as received)
tx.rx.decoded.ok: The test advertisement was decoded ({n} packets, {bad} CRC failures)
tx.rx.decoded.no: The test advertisement was not decoded ({n} packets, {bad} CRC failures)
tx.rx.clipped: The received signal is too strong (clipping). Lower the receive gain or add attenuation.
tx.rx.overflows: Reception was interrupted {n} times (the computer could not keep up with the device). It has little effect on the result; a lower sample rate reduces it.
tx.rx.reason.too_short: The received capture is too short to compare. Try a longer receive length.
tx.rx.reason.no_reference: There is no reference waveform to compare with.
tx.rx.spectrum.alt: Plot of received strength over frequency
tx.rx.how.tone: How it is judged: the highest point of the spectrum must be at the sent tone position and at least 15 dB above the floor (median). The vertical line marks the sent position.
tx.rx.how.waveform: How it is judged: the beginning of the sent waveform is cut into short pieces and aligned with the received signal (so a small frequency difference between devices is tolerated). 0.3 or more counts as received.
hub.ability.monitor.note: Monitor mode receives every frame nearby as-is, without connecting. This adapter supports it, but reading frames in monitor mode is not available in this tool yet.
home.task.monitor.desc: Receive nearby management frames (beacons, channel switch announcements and so on) as they are, without connecting
hub.mode.effect.monitor: The adapter {name} will drop its Wi-Fi connection and receive nearby frames as they are, without connecting. If you were using this adapter for internet access, it will be cut off. It only receives; nothing is sent.
hub.mode.effect.managed: The adapter {name} goes back to the state where it can connect to Wi-Fi as usual.
hub.mode.how.direct: The commands below will be run.
hub.mode.how.pkexec: The commands below will be run with administrator rights. The operating system will show a password prompt (this tool never receives the password).
hub.mode.how.manual: Administrator rights are needed but no authentication prompt is available. Run the commands below in a terminal yourself.
hub.mode.agree: I understand this adapter's connection will drop, and I am doing this on my own device.
hub.mode.no.macos: On macOS monitor mode is only on while capturing, so there is no button to switch it in advance.
hub.mode.no.unsupported: This adapter does not support monitor mode.
nearby.perm.ask: Ask for permission to show names
nearby.perm.asking: Choose in the operating system's prompt…
nearby.perm.opened: The settings window is open. Turn on this program (Terminal or Python) in the list, then press 'Once more now'.
nearby.perm.after: Allow this program (Terminal) in the settings, then reopen the program.
nearby.perm.location.undetermined: This program has not asked for location permission yet. If you ask, the operating system shows a prompt. This tool does not read your location; the permission is only needed to see network names.
nearby.perm.location.denied: Location permission is denied. Turn on this program (Terminal or Python) in the list in the settings window.
nearby.perm.location.restricted: Location permission is restricted on this computer and cannot be changed.
nearby.perm.location.off: Location Services is turned off. Turn it on in the settings window.
nearby.perm.location.authorized: Location permission is granted but names are still hidden. Try reopening the program.
nearby.perm.location.unknown: Could not read the permission state. Check it in the settings window.
home.simlink.title: Try it in simulation
home.simlink.lead: No device needed. Follow a base station to the end with practice signals or files you saved earlier.
home.pro_hint: Plug-and-use USRP support (automatic registration, reception, Wi-Fi decoding, transmit) is part of Pro. Pro is not installed here.
hub.needs_pro: Using this device requires the Pro edition. Contact: smjgallery.kr · mjseo@smjgallery.kr
home.tasks.pro: What Pro can do with this device
tx.plugin.frames.hint: This is a frame generator. The Wi-Fi frame bytes it returns get a checksum (FCS) appended and are turned into a 20 MHz non-HT waveform, sent repeatedly.
hub.ability.gpsdo.yes: A GPS module is fitted. This device can use a GPS-disciplined reference and time (choosing GPS as the reference is not available in this tool yet).
hub.ability.gpsdo.no: No GPS module is fitted. If the device accepts an external reference, a GPS-disciplined 10 MHz / PPS can be fed into its reference port.
hub.ref.title: Reference
hub.ref.unlocked: Not locked to the reference. Check the cable and signal level
hub.ref.unknown: The device did not report lock status
hub.ref.gps_unlocked: Not locked to GPS yet (check that the antenna sees the sky; the first lock takes minutes)
hub.ref.hint.external: Feed 10 MHz (and PPS) into the reference port. With the same signals on two devices and both set to External, their frequency and time agree.
hub.ref.hint.gpsdo: Uses the reference and time from the GPS module fitted to the device. A GPS antenna must be connected.
view.bands.hint: Pick a band to fill the fields below, then press Look. If it is wider than the device can receive, only the middle part is shown.
view.band.name: Name (blank: the frequency)
view.band.add_hint: Enter a centre frequency and bandwidth below, give it a name and add it. It is saved in this browser.
spectrum.look_picked: Put the picked range into the look fields
view.save.hint: Writes the received I/Q samples as they are to a SigMF file (.sigmf-data and .sigmf-meta) in the project's sessions/saved folder.
live.hint: Receive live: receives without gaps until you stop and keeps drawing. On a Wi-Fi channel (20 MHz) or a Bluetooth advertising channel (4 MHz) the matching decoder runs too. Record: saves the received I/Q samples from that moment to a SigMF file in the folder below until pressed again (up to 4 GB per file). Look once: receives 0.1 s and shows one picture.
live.gapped: This device cannot receive without gaps, so there are gaps between segments
live.wifi.title: Nearby APs ({channel})
live.ble.title: Nearby Bluetooth devices (advertising channel {channel})
live.caption.waterfall: Spectrogram: left is {s} s ago, right is now. Low frequencies at the bottom, darker is stronger.
home.what: ② What to do ({n} device(s) picked)
home.what.hint: Receive or Transmit opens the workbench. You choose the frequency and what to send there.
home.what.many: Each picked device gets its own pane side by side. Each pane can be switched between receive and transmit, so one device can send while another receives.
home.task.rx.desc: SDRs receive a chosen frequency (spectrogram, live receive, Wi-Fi and Bluetooth decoding, recording). The computer's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth show nearby networks and devices.
bench.empty: No panes yet. Pick devices on the home screen and press Receive or Transmit.
bench.gone: This device is not connected right now.
bench.hint: Set up each device on its tab, then press Start all: the overview shows every device's results side by side. Devices keep running while hidden.
bench.together.title: Start the transmit panes together
bench.together.lead: Starts every device at the same time with the values written in the transmit panes. The warning is confirmed on every start.
bench.together.incomplete: {n} transmit pane(s) are not fully filled in and will be left out.
bench.together.warn: The {n} devices below will transmit at the same time. Check the frequency and gain of each.
bench.together.aligned.pps: The devices started on a common time signal (external PPS or GPS).
bench.together.aligned.host: The computer set the device clocks before starting. Devices may differ by a few ms. For tighter alignment give each device an external reference (10 MHz and PPS).
home.devices.lead: Turn devices on or off. SDRs and this computer's Wi-Fi and Bluetooth appear together.
hub.search.cleaned: Stopped {n} process(es) that may have been holding the device.
view.target: Looking at: centre {c} MHz · width {w} MHz
view.target.none: Pick a place to look, or enter a centre frequency and bandwidth.
view.target.clipped: The picked range is wide, so only the middle {mhz} MHz is shown.
live.wifi.some: Decoded {m} of {n} frames found. The channel is busy, so an evenly spread share that fits in time is decoded. Record and decode later to cover everything.
live.scope.caption: Top: level per frequency now. The dark line is the mean, the light line the peak at that moment, and the shaded bands with numbers are found signals (numbers match the table below). Bottom: spectrogram. Horizontal is the same frequency axis, vertical is time (top is now), darker is stronger. {n} rows per second, shading from {lo} to {hi} dBFS.
signal.title: Signals seen now
signal.none: Nothing stands clearly above the floor yet.
signal.note: The kind is a guess from width and band only. An entry under 'Confirmed by decoding' means frames of that signal were actually decoded. Seen is the share of the last 5 s in which the signal appeared.
signal.dc: The sharp spike at the centre frequency leaks from the device itself and is left out of the table.
live.wifi.no_aps: No beacon decoded yet. Beacons come about every 0.1 s, but on a busy channel only part of the frames are decoded, so it can take a while.
job.label: What this pane does
job.live.hint: Receives one band continuously, draws it, labels the kind of signal by its shape, and records. Works for any signal.
job.levels.hint: Measures several places in turn and compares them as bars. In a band with channels it compares the picked channels; elsewhere it splits the entered range into slots. Save a baseline to see what rose above normal.
bench.idle_note: Not receiving yet. Set where to look on this device's tab, then press Start all.
view.out_of_range: This device can tune from {lo} to {hi} MHz. Check that the value is in MHz.
saved.path: Full path of the folder to save to
saved.export.done: Created ({mb} MB). The original is unchanged.
saved.export.note: This format carries no description. Enter sample rate {rate} MS/s and centre frequency {center} MHz in the program that opens it.
job.decode.hint: If a decoder fits the band, decodes the signal and shows what it carries. Available now: Wi-Fi (beacons → nearby APs) and Bluetooth LE (advertising → nearby devices). More decoders can be added.
levels.by_channels: Compares the level of the picked channels.
levels.by_range: Splits the range entered above into equal slots and measures each one.
levels.need: Pick channels, or enter a centre frequency and bandwidth.
decode.wifi: Wi-Fi (reads beacons to find nearby APs)
decode.ble: Bluetooth LE (reads advertising to find nearby devices)
decode.ble.find: Find nearby devices on the advertising channels
decode.none: There is no decoder for this band yet.
decode.need: Pick a band, or enter a centre frequency and bandwidth, to look for a matching decoder.
decode.tap.ok: fits this band (runs while you receive in the live view)
decode.none.hint: For signals without a decoder (remotes, car keys and so on) the live view labels the kind by width and position, and you can record them to decode with another tool.
tune.hint: Click the picture to receive again with that frequency in the centre.
home.task.analyze.desc: Open a recorded I/Q file and take the signals apart one by one. No device needed
analyze.title: Signal analysis
analyze.lead: Open a recorded I/Q file and see when, at which frequency and in what shape the signals appeared.
analyze.files.title: Choose a file
analyze.files.none: No recordings in the save folder ({folder}). Record from the receive screen, or choose a file below.
analyze.formats: SigMF (.sigmf-meta + .sigmf-data) carries its sample rate and frequency. For raw I/Q (.cfile · .cf32 · .iq are 32-bit float, .cs16 · .sc16 are 16-bit integer) enter the sample rate. Files are read in place on this computer (nothing is uploaded or copied).
analyze.over.title: Whole file · {name}
analyze.over.facts: Length {s} · centre {center} MHz · {rate} MS/s · {type} · scanned in {scan} s
analyze.over.sparse: long file, drawn sparsely (short signals all appear in the level line below)
analyze.over.caption: Top: spectrogram (time across, frequency up, darker is stronger). Bottom: level over time (dark line is the strongest value at that moment, faint line the mean). Drag across a picture to look at that span.
analyze.bursts.title: {n} bursts found
analyze.bursts.none: No on-off signals found. Either the signal is on the whole time or the recording is quiet. Drag across the picture to choose a span.
analyze.detail.title: A span in detail
analyze.detail.cut: Save just this span to a file
analyze.detail.coarse: The span is long, so only the level is shown. Narrow it to see the waveform, instantaneous frequency and constellation.
analyze.detail.heat_hint: Drag across to zoom into that span. The band marks the picked frequency.
analyze.detail.spectrum_hint: Click to pick that frequency, drag to pick a width too. Dark line is the mean, faint line the maximum. One bin {bin}
analyze.mod.psk: Steady level and frequency (PSK or bare carrier)
analyze.mod.ook.why: The level switches on and off. The lengths of on and off carry the 0s and 1s. With a wide pick other signals can mix in and mislead this.
analyze.mod.fsk.why: While on, the level is steady and the instantaneous frequency moves between two values. Half their difference is the deviation.
analyze.mod.psk.why: Level and frequency are both steady. If the constellation gathers in a few spots it is phase keyed; one spot (or a ring) is a bare carrier.
analyze.plot.freq.note: How fast the phase turns between neighbouring samples. Left blank where the signal is off. A frequency-keyed signal looks like steps here.
analyze.plot.constellation.note: I across, Q up. Samples taken while the signal is on. A ring means the frequency is slightly off: use 'Pick this signal' to centre it.
analyze.notice: This measures and shows shapes only. It does not demodulate to bits or interpret content. Use it to study your own devices and public signals.
tx.pick.place: A place you saved on the receive screen. Only the centre frequency is filled in. The confirmation dialog shows the frequency and power again before anything is sent.
analyze.mod.unpicked: press 'Pick this signal' for a guess
analyze.mod.unpicked.why: The full received width mixes noise and other signals, which blurs the shape. Click the signal in the spectrum, or use 'Pick this signal', to keep only that signal: the waveform, instantaneous frequency and constellation sharpen and the modulation is guessed.
